headline: Wheel-thrown stoneware for dining rooms and architectural interiors.
subline: Small-batch vessels, tableware, and ceramic lighting thrown and reduction-fired at 1,260°C in Melle.

craftStages.title: Raw Clay & Wedging
craftStages.description: Westerwald buff stoneware and iron-flecked grog clays are blended, spiral-wedged by hand to remove air pockets, and rested under damp linen before throwing.
details: 12% fine chamotte grog for structural stability
Zero synthetic plasticizers or commercial stains
Reclaimed trimmings slaked and recycled in-house

craftStages.title: Wheel Throwing & Trimming
craftStages.description: Each vessel and plate is thrown on a momentum wheel, dried slowly on raw pine boards, and turned at leather-hard stage to carve crisp architectural foot rings.
details: Hand-turned unglazed foot rings stamped with batch mark
Calibrated wall thickness for thermal retention
Slow ambient drying to prevent rim warping

craftStages.title: Bisque & Mineral Glazing
craftStages.description: Bisque-fired ware is dipped or poured with studio-formulated wood-ash, feldspar, and iron-oxide glazes mixed from raw mineral powders.
details: Beechwood ash washed and sieved through 80-mesh
Raw exterior clay left exposed on select vessels

craftStages.title: Reduction Firing
craftStages.description: Gas reduction firing draws oxygen from iron particles inside the clay body, producing warm toasted speckles and subtle tonal variation across every kiln shelf.
details: Cone 9–10 vitrification for zero water absorption
Numbered batch archive recorded per firing
